## Synopsis

```text
perch mail list [OPTIONS]
```

## Description

List mailboxes on the selected IMAP server. The default output is a table; --json writes one JSON object per line.

Aliases: `ls`.

## Notes

- --subscribed requires server support for LIST-EXTENDED.

## Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--username, -u <value>` | account username (env PERCH_IMAP_USER) |
| `--password <value>` | account password (prefer PERCH_IMAP_PASSWORD or --password-file) |
| `--password-file <value>` | read the account password from a file |
| `--password-stdin` | read the account password from stdin |
| `--timeout <value>` | connection timeout (default: 30s) |
| `--config <value>` | configuration file (default: ~/.config/perch/perch.yaml) |
| `--json` | write one JSON object per mailbox |
| `--subscribed` | only list subscribed mailboxes |
| `--server, -s <value>` | IMAP server (imaps://host, imap://host, or host[:port]); defaults from --config |
| `--plaintext` | connect to IMAP without TLS (use only on trusted networks) |
| `--starttls` | require STARTTLS for IMAP |
| `--insecure` | skip IMAP TLS certificate verification |
| `--ca-file <value>` | PEM CA bundle used to verify the IMAP server certificate |
| `--help, -h` | show help |

## Examples

```sh
perch mail list --server 127.0.0.1:1143 --plaintext --username you@example.com

perch mail list --server imaps://mail.example.com --username you@example.com --json
```

## Environment

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `PERCH_IMAP_USER` | default account username |
| `PERCH_IMAP_PASSWORD` | account password |
